items.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: The interviewee refers to Lucille as 'Louis’ wife' and 'Mrs. Armstrong', and mentions being left in charge of the legacy by 'Louis Armstrong and Lucille', indicating a professional/curatorial relationship to the Armstrong estate rather than a personal one with Lucille herself.

ctx.x: Switching subjects a little bit, perhaps you can, Phoebe you can help me out with this, you know I’ve been looking through a seemingly endless supply of Louis Armstrong records and I often wondered how did he learn so many songs to be — how did he record so much music? Did you ever witness him learning?

Yes. I witnessed Louis learning. Louis’ life was music. His dedication and his passion was performing. He lived to entertain people. It was effortless for him. It was like breathing. He told his wife Lucille, who he adored, you’ve got to understand, Mama, my horn comes first, and she understood and she never was jealous of his horn. But that was Louis. It was effortless for him to learn. But he’d go in a place, well that’s how scat singing started, because he lost the music that was on the music stand but he…
Would he sit with the pianist perhaps and learn the tune that way? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
